# proxmox_node_network_revert (Resource)

Discards the staged network configuration of one Proxmox VE node through `DELETE /nodes/{node}/network` and waits for the worker task. Proxmox reverts the whole node at once, so this drops every staged interface change, not one interface. Destroy is a no-op: an applied configuration stays applied. A failed revert keeps the instance in state for a retry.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# Discards every staged change of the node. Proxmox reverts per node, so this
# drops all pending interface edits, not just the ones of one resource.
resource "proxmox_node_network_revert" "node1_staged" {
  node = "node1"

  triggers = {
    staged = sha1(jsonencode(proxmox_node_network_interface.vmbr7))
  }

  # Revert before the apply so the reload below picks up the reverted state.
  depends_on = [proxmox_node_network_interface.vmbr7]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node` (String) Cluster node whose staged configuration is discarded. Changes require replacement.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values that decide when another revert is due; changing any of them reverts again. Use something that changes when the staged configuration does, for example `{ staged = sha1(jsonencode(proxmox_node_network_apply.this.pending_changes)) }`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Revert identifier (the node name).
- `pending_changes` (List of String) Staged changes Proxmox still reports for the node. Empty after a successful revert.
